sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct PhD entry does not require a master's. Bachelor's completion and adequate preparation remain
necessary. [s1] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Create the graduate application account; arrange institutional transcripts and three referees. Resolve the
mathematics-specific English waiver before assuming UChicago study exempts testing. [s1] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact graduate associate chair Lee Kennard, ltkennar@syr.edu, for admission/fit questions; no supervisor
commitment is listed. [s1]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Department links the central graduate application; do not send application materials to the mathematics
department. [s2]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Main page explicitly updated to 2027 application deadline; FAQ retains 2026 entry and older stipend. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
The main mathematics page requires TOEFL for international applicants, self-reported and officially sent by
ETS using Syracuse code 2823. The FAQ supplies the US-degree exception, states no minimum score and
describes 100 as a typical successful score on the older 0-120 scale, not an absolute threshold. A mathematics
threshold under the new 2026 TOEFL scale was not published. Spoken English is separately assessed for
teaching. [s1] [qafaq]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
The mathematics FAQ explicitly permits a TOEFL waiver for someone holding a degree from a US institution.
Thus a completed UChicago degree fits the stated route; applying before conferral and the request/approval
procedure remain unresolved. The FAQ still carries Fall 2026 headings, so obtain current confirmation before
omitting scores for Fall 2027. Admission waiver does not establish spoken-English clearance for TA duties.
[qafaq]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not considered. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional; omission not penalized. If submitted, include score in CV or statement. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Published 2026-27 TA stipend: USD 29,500, plus tuition scholarship up to 24 credits/academic year. 2027-28
amount unannounced. [s1]
Years of support [Standing rule]
The FAQ says assistantship/fellowship offers guarantee six years of support subject to acceptable academic
progress. Its dated admissions headings concern Fall 2026; confirm the same duration in the Fall 2027 offer.
[qafaq]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants can receive assistantships; spoken-English teaching clearance matters. [s2]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
TA workload: 20 hours/week; clearance to teach required. Summer support is not guaranteed. [s1] [s2]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No additional application for standard departmental assistantships/fellowships; separate scholarship prompts
or references are not listed. [s2]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Continuing students may receive summer TA/fellowship support (recently above USD 4,000 average);
advanced-student RAs depend on grants. The FAQ describes summer TA/fellowship support for continuing
students after at least one semester, historically averaging USD 3,700-4,000; it is not guaranteed because
courses can be cancelled. This amount is not a verified 2027 summer offer. [s1] [qafaq]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 75, nonrefundable, payable by credit card; most major cards accepted. [qafee]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
A Syracuse policy published by Maxwell explicitly says these automatic waivers apply regardless of graduate
program: US military/veterans, Syracuse students/alumni, McNair Scholars (faculty research-mentor
recommendation), international Fulbright scholars through IIE/AMIDEAST/LASPAU, and applicants from Israel,
Palestine and Ukraine for 2027 admission. Select the relevant application responses. Other affiliation or
hardship waivers depend on the department; no mathematics-specific hardship process or deadline was

verified. Start the application before requesting a nonautomatic waiver. UChicago enrollment/F-1 status alone
is not listed as qualifying. [qawaiver]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Graham J. Leuschke
Cohen-Macaulay representation theory, matrix factorizations and noncommutative resolutions. [s4] [s5]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Characteristic-free Knörrer periodicity
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Steven P. Diaz
Algebraic geometry of families of curves; an older institutional paper also concerns preprojective algebras and
multiplication maps. A recent dated paper was not established. [s4] [s7] [q10]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2005 · Almost Split Morphisms, Preprojective Algebras and Multiplication Maps of Maximal Rank
Research-paper evidence. Publication year is as stated; an old paper is not proof of recent activity.
Complex geometry
Dan Coman
Complex geometry and pluripotential theory; asymptotics of holomorphic bundles, Chern forms, and random
degeneracy sets on compact Kähler manifolds. [s4] [s6] [q9]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Asymptotic expansion of induced Grassmannian Chern forms and distribution of random
degeneracy sets
Research-paper evidence. Publication year is as stated; an old paper is not proof of recent activity.

Representation theory
Claudia Miller
Commutative and homological algebra, differential operators on singularities, matrix factorizations and
algebraic geometry. [s4] [s8] [q11]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Resolutions of Differential Operators of Low Order for an Isolated Hypersurface Singularity
Research-paper evidence. Publication year is as stated; an old paper is not proof of recent activity.
Representation theory / commutative algebra
Josh Pollitz
Homological commutative algebra, support theories and resolutions, with links to triangulated categories and
representation theory. [a12] [a12p]
Current departmental faculty; accepting new doctoral students is not confirmed publicly.
Research evidence: 2026 · High Frobenius pushforwards generate the bounded derived category
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.

English requirement [Standing rule]
The main mathematics page requires TOEFL for international applicants, self-reported and officially sent by
ETS using Syracuse code 2823. The FAQ supplies the US-degree exception, states no minimum score and
describes 100 as a typical successful score on the older 0-120 scale, not an absolute threshold. A mathematics
threshold under the new 2026 TOEFL scale was not published. Spoken English is separately assessed for
teaching. [s1] [qafaq]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]

procedure remain unresolved. The FAQ still carries Fall 2026 headings, so obtain current confirmation before
omitting scores for Fall 2027. Admission waiver does not establish spoken-English clearance for TA duties.

Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
A Syracuse policy published by Maxwell explicitly says these automatic waivers apply regardless of graduate
program: US military/veterans, Syracuse students/alumni, McNair Scholars (faculty research-mentor
recommendation), international Fulbright scholars through IIE/AMIDEAST/LASPAU, and applicants from Israel,
Palestine and Ukraine for 2027 admission. Select the relevant application responses. Other affiliation or
hardship waivers depend on the department; no mathematics-specific hardship process or deadline was

verified. Start the application before requesting a nonautomatic waiver. UChicago enrollment/F-1 status alone
is not listed as qualifying. [qawaiver]
